name: Djupvik
description: A private housing project completed in 2023, designed by Arrhov Frick Arkitektkontor AB.

name: Väddö Veda
description: A private house project with a built area between 40-120 m2, currently under construction.

name: AF. 180 / GRISSLEHAMN / 1809
description: A private house proposal with a flexible area range of 40-120 m2.

name: Villa Toivonen
description: A 140 m² private house completed in Norrtälje, Sweden.

name: Atelier Lapidus
description: A 150 m² private house completed in 2016-2017, though specific materials and architectural features are not detailed in the available text.

name: Viggsö
description: A private house with a total area of 80 square meters, composed of three distinct sections of 40, 20, and 20 square meters.

name: Bredören
description: A private house of 80 m² designed by Arrhov Frick Arkitektkontor AB and documented through sketches and photographs by Mikael Olsson.

name: Lilla Rågholmen
description: A 100 square meter private house completed in the Stockholm Archipelago.

name: AF. 52 / NYKVARN / 1209
description: A private house with a total area of 145 square meters (100 + 30 + 15 m²) completed in 2014.

name: Townhouse
description: A narrow townhouse on a constrained site between old neighboring buildings, featuring three thin interior slabs that divide the open volume while maintaining continuous space that opens to the street, an intimate garden, and the sky.

name: Århus
description: A winning competition proposal for a townhouse on Jaegergårdsgade in Aarhus, Denmark.

name: House with a hidden atrium
description: A detached extension to a 1950s cabin featuring four volumes of varying heights arranged around a hidden central atrium, with blackened pine exterior cladding and plywood interior walls with strategically placed windows framing tree tops.

name: House in a horse field
description: A single-family house informed by rural farm buildings, positioned on a sloping site to offer panoramic views of Lake Vättern, with rooms arranged on stepped levels following the terrain and organized around a central vertical core containing the stairwell and wet rooms.

name: House with rope and ladder
description: A house in two parts consisting of a traditional brick volume with a gable roof and an enclosed circular garden, designed to create a calm private space while overlooking the sea on Sweden's southeast coast.

name: House for two artists
description: An extension to an older villa with a square footprint and cinderblock walls, featuring free-spanning glulam beams and sixteen skylights to create a flexible open atelier space, with pitch black tar felt cladding on the exterior contrasting the bright interior.

name: House for mother
description: A single-family dwelling and studio featuring a corrugated aluminum facade with wooden beams, plywood-lined walls, and concrete flooring, organized as two parallel gabled volumes that shift to emphasize the narrow plot.

name: House on Two Stairs
description: A narrow single-family house elevated on steel legs and balanced on two cast-in-place concrete stairs, featuring seven equally sized rooms separated by cross-laminated timber walls, with untreated wood panel and sheet metal roofing.

name: Surbrunnsgatan
description: A transformed 50 m² brick workshop converted into a small home featuring a partial second floor with exposed wood beams, Douglas veneer shelving, concrete flooring, and a deep green kitchen with whitewashed wood elements.

name: X
description: A competition entry for a modular house with a square footprint divided by a central X into four equal rooms, constructed from cross-laminated timber delivered as self-supported elements for on-site assembly.

name: Fritidshus i Tänndalen
description: A 130 sqm vacation house in the mountains with three bedrooms, a large living room with fireplace and valley views, plus a snowmobile garage and ski storage, featuring traditional Härjedalen-inspired interiors with green ceiling details and red woodwork combined with modern design.

name: Fritidshus i Bruksvallarna
description: A small vacation house with a timber upper volume in the X House system, iron vitriol-treated wooden facade, and a separate building for snowmobile storage, featuring sleeping loft, sauna, kitchen, and gathering spaces.

name: Bostadshus i Jämtlandsfjällen
description: A new red residential house in a mountain landscape that references the proportions and character of a previous dwelling on the site, with modern window placements and spatial arrangements designed for a family living close to nature.

name: Undrom
description: A modern vacation house with wood architecture, sedum roof, and extensive glazing toward the landscape, featuring 2.8-meter ceiling heights, concrete floors, and an iron vitriol-treated limber-clad facade.

name: The Dune Cabin
description: A low-lying summer house with a post-and-beam structure featuring corten steel infill panels, sawn pine walls, polished concrete floors, and discrete glass elements that blur the boundary between interior and exterior.

name: Villa Butter
description: A heavy, modern villa situated on a cliff overlooking the ocean and within a grove, designed with oak, concrete, glass, and copper materials, featuring a blurred boundary between interior and exterior spaces with deep blue accents.

name: STENEN&ENEN
description: A raw experimental house featuring stones and junipers in a foggy setting, for which the firm prepared building permits, construction drawings, and executed the project.

name: Ö17
description: A house for an art collector designed as a formalized vision integrating architecture and art, situated within an old stone quarry on Gotland with spaces that function as a gallery, featuring a material palette balanced between perfection and imperfection that frames views and creates tectonic phenomena.

name: Djupvike
description: An artist's combined home and studio compound of five single-story structures featuring concrete, treated pine wood, and plaster, with playful interior details including pink apricot marble terrazzo and blue painted ceilings, positioned on a rocky cove overlooking the Baltic Sea.

name: Savannen 8
description: A rectangular house built from prefabricated concrete walls with raw concrete and plywood interiors, featuring a facade created through a custom method developed with a local concrete factory and incorporating industrial-inspired details like a kitchen fan made from a galvanized steel foot grate.

name: Villa Fjällsvik
description: A private villa on a rocky archipelago island featuring a modest sea-facing façade that replaces a former cottage, with a larger northwestern wing tucked into the landscape, designed with materials and craftsmanship inspired by the seaside context.

name: Sahara
description: A summer cottage built from local materials by local artisans, elevated on light stilts over the forest floor with a pine facade, designed as a simple yet sophisticated structure in the threshold between forest and sea.

name: Villa BM
description: A summer house designed as an enclosed courtyard villa that creates a sense of seclusion and intimacy, with tall pine trees from the surrounding forest visible above the property walls, making the residence feel isolated within the forest.

name: Pine House
description: A summer house completed in 2024 featuring a visible timber construction with handcrafted detailing, sited on a north-facing slope in sparse forest and designed to honor authentic, tactile experiences through natural materials and legible structural expression.

name: Sommarhus S
description: A summer house completed in 2025, designed by Johan Sundberg Arkitektur with carpentry by Kasper Thulin.

name: Villa HDV
description: A family home featuring contrasting materials that express varying degrees of intimacy, surrounded by carefully planned garden rooms and landscape on all sides.

name: Sommarhus E
description: A single-family vacation house on Gotland built with local wood, glass, limestone, and concrete in a Nordic mid-century bungalow style that sits low to the ground and uses narrow ribbons of slow-growth pine to integrate with its natural surroundings.

name: BV50
description: A modern family home in a coastal pine forest designed with a unified material palette of brick, glass, wood, and Baltic limestone, featuring flexible spaces that adapt as the family grows and carefully balanced transitions between shared and private areas.

name: Yngsjö
description: A family summer house for four people featuring a north-south oriented volume with a sheltered western terrace, with the southern section grounded and the northern section elevated on slender pillars, clad in larch panel with oak interior finishes and larch ceiling.

name: Villa MSV
description: A residence designed for a couple with accommodations for guests and family, positioned among tall pine forest with two distinct garden spaces oriented to morning sun and west-facing areas for sitting and dining.

name: Sommarhus Solviken
description: A three-bedroom summer house elevated on twelve steel columns on a steep slope with sea views, featuring wood facade panels, muted green tones, black-lacquered aluminum windows and doors, and large sliding glass doors opening to a wraparound balcony.

name: Sommarhus T
description: A summer house for a family with two children composed of three interconnected volumes with a large shared shallow hipped roof, featuring a timber frame with steel elements and natural larch and stained spruce, designed to appear modest from outside while providing generous interior spaces and nature contact in all directions.

name: Villa Tennisvägen
description: A family residence designed as two brick volumes and one aluminum-clad volume arranged in a U-shape around an inner courtyard, featuring black brick, dark gray aluminum, oak and cedar wood interiors, and natural stone accents.

name: Sommarhus H
description: A vacation house on the south coast of Skåne, clad in specially designed larch wood panel treated with silicate-based wood protection, featuring shadow play from battens on the facades and opening toward water views with separate compartments of varying depth and window placement.

name: Villa J
description: A generous family villa with three children's bedrooms featuring a central atrium courtyard, with a timber and steel frame structure and facades clad in Danish brick, light gray plaster, dark-stained pine, and black-painted aluminum.

name: Bergman-Werntoft
description: A private residence inspired by traditional Scanian-Danish atrium houses, featuring a masonry exterior wall and largely glazed interior façade, with steel-reinforced timber construction on a concrete slab, black-painted light concrete walls, and Siberian larch cladding, designed to blur the boundary between interior and nature through a year-round winter garden and flush floor transitions.

name: Villa Syrstad
description: A family residence designed in harmony with its coastal landscape, featuring generous glazing on the west and south facades, covered terraces, and a brick fireplace dividing the living spaces, with private bedroom areas at each end.

name: Sommarhus Akenine
description: A summer house nestled in the forest on the south coast of Skåne, Sweden, featuring a distinctive timber deck structure resting on three concrete beams, with light timber and glass walls clad in Siberian larch panels and three-layer lamellar boards, designed to open toward the sea while providing shelter from the forest side.

name: Sommarhus Sandby
description: A 167 m² summer house for a family of five with wood-clad façades and roof in treated Siberian larch, featuring open-plan living spaces with sliding glass walls that connect to the surrounding forest and garden.

name: Villa Ljung
description: A residential villa on a double plot near the sea, consisting of three timber-clad buildings with facades of Siberian larch in varying qualities, Danish hard-fired tile floors, and rooms organized around a large central living space with a fireplace and adjoining winter garden.

name: Villa Lima
description: A 1.5-story modern villa with a traditional pitched roof, featuring large glass sections, dark gray matte facade with mixed-width smooth-planed wood, steel-reinforced timber construction, and an open floor plan that preserves existing trees on the property.

name: Villa Håkansson-Tegman
description: A single-story modern house designed around an inner courtyard with Danish atrium house origins, clad in light Danish brick with a steel-reinforced timber frame, featuring extensive window placements and aluminum profiles to maximize connection with nature and light.

name: House V
description: A three-level private home on a cliff overlooking Djurgården featuring exposed cast-in-place concrete and dark brick exterior, with oak floors and limestone interiors, organized with open living spaces on the top level and more intimate rooms below.

name: House on a Hill
description: A three-level private residence entirely cast in concrete and anchored to exposed bedrock, featuring a distinctive rotated floor plan with folded facades that create wind-shielded terraces and origami-like visual effects while merging indoor and outdoor spaces to emphasize views over the Stockholm archipelago.

name: House on a Hillside
description: A private home laid out as six stepped and staggered blocks that follow the natural topography, featuring exposed concrete blocks (referencing local barn construction) with large infrequent window openings and a linear interior passage connecting varied spatial sequences.

name: Garden House
description: A 180 m² wooden private home on a Mälaren lakefront site with a triangular footprint driven by topography, wrapped in a trellis supporting vines and seven plant species to create vertical gardens, featuring a two-storey winter garden and open-plan ground floor with a roof terrace.

name: Archipelago House
description: A lightweight 130 m² summer vacation house in wood and glass with a black-stained exterior, white-painted interior, and extensive glazing that creates reflective interactions between interior space and the surrounding archipelago landscape.

name: Red House
description: A private residence with a symmetrical pitched roof and Falu red-stained wooden façade, featuring a solid Swedish timber load-bearing structure and layered plywood panels that create a three-dimensional shingle-like effect, designed to complement the early 18th-century cultural heritage buildings on the site while offering contemporary living spaces inside.

name: Atrium House
description: A vacation home built as a low wall around an enclosed atrium courtyard, featuring masonry with natural plaster tinted with carbon black, oxidised zinc metal components, and tar oil-treated oak doors and windows that grey naturally over time.

name: Husarö
description: A vacation home with a pitched roof and open spatial plan, clad entirely in folded black sheet metal, with wood construction including glulam beams and plywood vaults, positioned on a clearing overlooking the sea in the Stockholm archipelago.

name: Engberga - ThamVidegård
description: A three-level private home on a Stockholm archipelago peninsula featuring a solid concrete base, a glazed middle floor with open pillars, and a top floor clad in burnt wood (Shou sugi ban), organized around curved concrete walls and a central wooden box containing stairs, fireplace, and storage.

name: House K
description: A thin residential block in Stocksund featuring cut-outs for light, double-height voids, and a roof terrace, with façades of stained black plywood panels mounted on a slow-grown pine framework and an exposed concrete entrance canopy.

name: Söderöra
description: A lightweight summer house on a remote Stockholm archipelago island built from wood and glass materials transported by boat, organized around a top-lit central room with four corner rooms and finished with black bitumen slate roof and natural wooden panels.

name: Villa Gislöv
description: A single-floor seaside villa with brick walls providing rhythm and stability, a flat lightweight roof with overhangs for sun protection, and strategically placed glass and wood sections that maximize southern views while providing privacy toward the north and courtyard.

name: Villa Siblings
description: Two sister houses with a shared central concrete wall and solid timber frame, featuring free-form geometry, open family rooms with varying ceiling heights, and minimalist interiors with unfinished wood and exterior larch cladding.

name: House Djurö
description: A cast in situ concrete house perched on a cliff overlooking the Stockholm Archipelago, featuring flanking walls that frame views toward the sea, stained spruce timber windows and doors, a large concrete terrace with frameless glass balustrade, a custom pool, and interiors with concrete walls and floors complemented by stained oak paneling and stainless steel kitchen elements.

name: Björhövda House
description: A private house in a forest clearing with a wooden facade clad in Organowood that grays over time, featuring a diagonal floor plan that creates unexpected spatial qualities and views toward a nearby lake and surrounding forest.

name: Smallholding at Nesjestranda
description: An extension and remodeling of a smallholding on Norway's northwest coast, featuring oiled dense pine cladding with tapered boards for filtered light, a stepped roofline clad in aluzinc that follows the terrain, and a new entrance with cast concrete flooring and wood stove heating.

name: Chr Tomters veg
description: An expansion of a traditional red-painted wooden house into a spatially complex residence for a large family, with two new volumes linked by transitional spaces and featuring a material palette of reds in timber cladding, brick, and tiles alongside interior finishes of ash wood, painted surfaces, brick, and concrete.

name: Cabin Nordmarka
description: A small retreat cabin with an open, light interior featuring a multi-level layout that ascends from entrance to living, recreational, sleeping, and children's areas, designed to minimize environmental impact through a steel bolt foundation system and positioned to maximize views of sunset, woods, and lakes while respecting an adjacent 1930s cabin.

name: Cabin Ulvik
description: A cabin designed as homage to country-road architecture, featuring ochre-yellow walls that camouflage into the aspen forest, a thick protective southern wall facing prevailing winds and rain, and a facade composition that blends vernacular farmhouse and barn design traditions.

name: Kvinaosen
description: A single family house designed by Rever & Drage AS in 2021.

name: Zieglers Nest
description: A tall, slender single-family house built on a steep site with a framework ground floor and log construction upper floors, featuring oak and pine staircases, south-facing views of the Molde fjord panorama, and a five-meter high utility room with flood lighting on the ground level.

name: 1/3 Hus
description: A detached single-family house with two insulated floors of 50 square meters each, featuring a large uninsulated utility space under an extended roof supported by tilted glulam columns, designed for affordability and future expandability as the owners' family grows.

name: Trolltind
description: A robust mountain cabin built with high-quality traditional craftmanship and local timber, arranged as a connected row of differently-constructed buildings featuring a glassed-in garage, laundry area, kitchen, living room with barrel vault ceiling and panorama window, bedrooms, and workspace, designed for active outdoor families with drying facilities and panoramic mountain views.

name: House Øksendal
description: A detached single-family house with a simple exterior and complex interior featuring a tractor and ATV garage, gym, cheese and wine cellar in the bedrock, wood-fired water heating system, and a kitchen with a five-meter-high ceiling and large south-facing windows, organized around a central staircase.

name: Cabin Årsund
description: A residential cabin combining a traditional gabled roof structure with modernist flat-roofed modules, featuring a sheltered main volume with bedrooms and a west-facing study module with ocean views, connected to a pre-existing annex.

name: Feisteinveien
description: An addition to a single-family house featuring a large northern extension with two small bedrooms, living room, and combined home-cinema-and-exercise room with classical skylight, along with a smaller southern extension for bathroom and entrance, designed to preserve the original building as the central element with contrasting color.

name: Pedervegen
description: An addition to a 1962 Scandinavian functionalist detached house featuring wood cladding in colors derived from the original brick walls, with quarter-circle forms and distinctly zoned bathroom and bedroom spaces designed to capture specific light and views of the surrounding mountains.

name: Furukollen
description: A single-family house for four people integrated between granite outcrops, featuring a coal-burned brick ground floor anchored to bedrock, a lightweight timber upper floor, a long ridge beam with clerestory window, and interior surfaces clad in knot-free pine panelling with custom Norwegian pine joinery.

name: Sykkylven
description: A single-storey building that meanders between trees, responding to the landscape, vegetation, and surrounding views.

name: Long House on Pillars
description: A 115 sqm residential house for a ceramicist and scientist, raised on wooden pillars to preserve the existing landscape, featuring exposed wooden beams and pine walls with recycled brick floors, set between rocks and trees with a simple open floor plan separated by sliding doors.

name: Brick house with tower
description: A 220 sqm single-family house with a tower featuring loadbearing wooden construction clad in coal-fired red, brown and ochre Danish brick, with copper fittings and ash windows, organized across three stories with long views through the interior and overlooking Lake Mjøsa.

name: House in Red Concrete
description: An intergenerational three-generation family home built with prefabricated red iron oxide-pigmented concrete elements designed for partial owner self-construction, featuring exposed concrete ceilings, pine paneling in the kitchen and living areas, and a flexible interior layout adapted to a steep hillside site.

name: Cabin Rones
description: A small residential cabin with a compact concrete base and triangular cross-laminated timber upper floor wrapped in black roofing felt, featuring raw concrete walls, polished concrete floors, Norwegian pine interiors, and an open glass facade facing the fjord.

name: Lofoten house
description: A single-family house with wood construction on a concrete base and steel cladding.

name: Corbus Nephew
description: Renovation and extension of a single-family house from 1940, allegedly built by Le Corbusier's nephew, Mr. Eduard Jaquet.

name: Atelier Aksnes
description: A self-built 20 sqm atelier designed for a ceramicist.

name: T House
description: A villa reinterpreting the traditional Trønderlåna with three wings creating two outdoor spaces, featuring a wooden frame construction in birch plywood and charred pine boards under an aluminium roof.

name: House14a
description: A 1951 post-war single-family house with red brick façade and gable roof, transformed through traditional architectural techniques like exposing, covering, cutting, and joining to create a non-hierarchical collage of old and new elements.

name: House on Fanø
description: A contemporary reinterpretation of the traditional Fanø longhouse that combines local building traditions with modern construction, featuring robust materials and sensory qualities while maintaining the east-west orientation and simple structure characteristic of the island's historic dwellings.

name: Sankt Knuds Vej
description: An extension on a private house in Frederiksberg designed in collaboration with office kim lenschow.

name: House in Mols Hills
description: A 175 sqm summer residence with four interconnected 'house-shaped' units around a central courtyard, featuring oiled cedar boards, sliding shutters, and floor-to-ceiling windows that blur interior-exterior boundaries.

name: Tagestorp
description: A private house in Gentofte designed by pihlmann in collaboration with office kim lenschow.

name: Villa Tambar
description: A 220 m² house featuring an inviting ground floor paired with a more secluded upper level to establish dedicated spaces for everyday life.

name: Garden House
description: A distinctive addition to a multi-generational home that encloses a shared courtyard anchored by a majestic oak tree, with a size of 160 m².

name: House at Nøtterøy
description: A new family house cut into the landscape that blends with its surroundings, with a size of 170 m².

name: A31-A
description: A compact family house of 123 m² where two spaces connected by a long wall make up the main living area.

name: Hus på Valderøya
description: A renovation and expansion of a 1973 villa featuring three cast concrete elements that shield from westerly winds, large glazed doors opening to views of Alnes lighthouse, and interior finishes in ash, solid oak, and pine combined with exposed laminated timber.

name: Hytte i Hol
description: A renovation and extension of a vacation house featuring a new addition with bedrooms and a separate living room, with matching wood panel and details that harmonize with the original structure and a sheltered outdoor area.

name: Green Villa Margo
description: A mass timber single-family house with CLT structures, dark-green-painted facades, zinc roof, natural ventilation, and interior finishes of light spruce and dark red terracotta tiles, designed to nestle around an existing knoll with preserved vegetation.

name: Palapa De Oro
description: Fourteen primitive yet luxurious holiday homes made in local clay and timber, offering space for silence, simplicity and relaxation.

name: Cubiculum
description: A timeless residential haven inspired by the Roman domus, featuring natural haptic materials of wood and clay in a technology-free environment designed for rest and peaceful living.

name: Villa in the archipelago
description: A holiday villa in the Finnish archipelago built with massive CLT wooden walls and slabs, featuring natural gravity ventilation, a detached foundation slab, visible bearing roof structure, and large windows creating a close relationship between interior and exterior spaces.

name: Villa Koppar
description: A fully ecological, geothermically heated passive house for a young family constructed with a prefabricated straw structure (Ecococon), featuring spruce board cladding, clay plaster interiors, rammed earth floors, and a roof with bio-based color-coated steel with rapeseed oil coating.

name: Villa Ris
description: A 320 square meter villa completed in 2025.

name: Villa Solveien
description: A 350 m² intimate family home designed for a steep hillside site, featuring a structural division of a heavy concrete base with light timber construction above, a central oak staircase, and materials chosen for durability and timeless quality.

name: Ullernkollen
description: A residential project of approximately 220 m² completed in 2024 in Oslo, designed by R21 Arkitekter AS.

name: Villa Berg
description: A 390 m² single-family house with a narrow facade to the street and elongated form following the terrain, featuring cast-in-place concrete with red pigment, red brick, copper, and oak materials, with an internal atrium bringing light through vertical connections.

name: Villa Nes Terrasse
description: A 350 m² single-family villa featuring a horizontal roof plane with integrated technical installations, closed wooden boxes defining interior spaces, and a gabion retaining wall that anchors the structure into the sloped terrain.

name: Villa Bruksveien
description: A 340 m² villa completed in 2024, designed by R21 Arkitekter AS.

name: Villa Bombakken
description: A 400 m² villa completed in 2022 in Lysaker, Bærum.

name: Villa Dagaliveien
description: A 550 m² villa completed in 2022, designed by R21 Arkitekter AS and built by Gunnar Johansson.

name: Villa Bjerkealleen
description: A compact rectangular house with a sloped roof, brick base and red-painted wood panel facade, featuring a central dining room, multiple living spaces, and outdoor terraces positioned on sloping terrain with two stories plus a basement level.

name: Villa Slemdalsvingen
description: A single-family house of 350 m² featuring brick façades with oak details and a volumetric form that responds to neighboring architecture while creating multi-level outdoor spaces oriented toward the south.

name: Villa Trosterudveien
description: A single-family home composed of four distinct volumes with pitched roofs, featuring concrete foundation, timber frame construction, standing wood cladding on façade and roof, with an attached garage and glass-clad greenhouse, designed to respect the scale of the surrounding residential area while adapting to the sloped terrain.

name: Villa Gyssestadkollen
description: A single-family house on a south-facing slope with two stories plus a basement level, featuring a triangular floor plan that optimizes views and noise protection, with concrete and white concrete construction in the atrium and dark copper cladding on the main floors.

name: Villa Snarøya
description: A approximately 350 m² villa with a pitched roof, positioned to maximize fjord views and southern light, featuring a façade that combines cedar wood, aluminum, and glass, with open-plan living spaces on the ground floor and bedroom areas on upper levels.

name: Hytte Budor
description: A 120 m² vacation house completed in 2025, designed by R21 Arkitekter AS.

name: 3PR Hytta
description: A compact 70 m² vacation cabin with loft space designed as a modular prototype that combines architectural quality, flexibility, and sustainability through a 3x3 unit planning system that can be mirrored and rotated to adapt to different sites and orientations.

name: Vinterro
description: A pair of cabins of 110 m² and 140 m² completed in 2024 at Kvitfjell.

name: Hytte Ostøya
description: A 110 m² vacation house completed in 2025, designed by R21 Arkitekter AS.

name: Hytte Nøtterøy
description: A 90 m² cabin completed in 2024, designed by R21 Arkitekter AS.

name: Hytte Kvitfjell
description: A 260 m² cabin completed in 2024, designed by R21 Arkitekter AS.

name: Hytte Portør
description: A 75 m² completed vacation house designed by R21 Arkitekter AS.

name: Sand Paviljong
description: An 80 m² pavilion-like cottage with exposed oak columns outside the glass façade, concrete foundation, flexible wooden shutters, and an open-air kitchen concept that can be fully opened in summer.

name: Haus am Wiesenweg
description: A single-family courtyard house with timber construction and an L-shaped footprint that prioritizes privacy, featuring a covered terrace, barrier-free ground-floor master suite, and upper-floor children's rooms.

name: House by the fens
description: A residential and studio building in the Bregenzerwald region with a longitudinal pitched roof design, featuring a concrete core zone, highly insulated external elements, and extensive use of locally-sourced wood (spruce, fir, and elm) for structural parts, walls, and flooring, along with handmade brick clay tiles incorporating floor heating.

name: House on Schopfacker
description: A two-family house with a granny flat featuring solid timber construction with a concrete core, wood-paneling interiors, and a hipped roof that references traditional Appenzell regional architecture while meeting modern living standards.

name: Haus Fontanella
description: A mountain house for a 6-member family featuring preassembled timber construction on a concrete and natural stone basement, with geothermal heating and a wood stove.

name: House in the field
description: A timber-constructed courtyard house with a pitched roof on a small corner plot, featuring an internalised courtyard with large sliding shutters framing Alpine views, wooden floors and paneling, and a low-energy standard with geothermal heating.

name: EMA Haus
description: A 90m² private residence featuring preassembled construction with high-level prefabrication and a geothermal heat pump heating system.

name: HD Haus
description: A house on a hill with timber element construction on a solid basement, heated by a heat pump with depth probe and wood stove.

name: Haus Fohren
description: A cottage for a retired couple and their guests built with modular, preassembled timber construction and heated by a wood stove and geothermal heat pump.

name: AMA Haus
description: A family house in Bregenzerwald with timber construction, geothermal heating, and 150m² of floor space, winning distinction awards for its design.

name: KR Haus
description: A massive timber house featuring a unique 'knitted' timber log-construction on a concrete base, with geothermal heat pump and wood stove for energy.

name: K Haus
description: A village house with timber element construction on a concrete base, featuring a geothermal heat pump with depth probe for energy.

name: Haus Salgenreute
description: An extension of a 1970s holiday home featuring timber element construction on a partial concrete basement with a wood stove for heating.

name: House Kaltschmieden
description: A single-storey house with gable roof and minimized formal language, built with a core zone in light concrete and perimeter structure in white fir timber, incorporating materials and components salvaged from the demolished original farmhouse that previously occupied the site.

name: House at the Stürcherwald
description: A modern interpretation of traditional Walser long-house farming architecture, featuring prefabricated wood elements with rough-sawn larch exterior panels and a compact, elongated form positioned on a steeply sloping mountain plot at 1000 meters elevation.

name: Haus für Julia und Björn
description: A single-family house that won multiple awards including the Houses of the Year 2015 and the Vorarlberg Timber Construction Prize 2015.

name: Haus mit Schauraum
description: A combined residential and commercial building on a narrow, exposed lot along a municipal road, featuring a showroom and office on the north facade with private residential spaces organized across two floors to the south.

name: Haus für Gudrun
description: A single-family house organized around a central core containing utilities and bathrooms, featuring a large living space, two small bedrooms, white spruce wood walls with integrated deep-set windows and built-in elements, and a central dark concrete core contrasting with the surrounding light wood.

name: Villa D
description: A villa designed by Architekten Innauer Matt in collaboration with Bernardo Bader Architekten, which won third prize in a 2015 competition.

name: Berghaus Eller
description: A three-story residential house designed with economic restraint, featuring a whole-house tiled stove for energy efficiency, locally-sourced timber materials, and a central living area with a tile stove as the family's social heart.

name: Ceangal House
description: A new five-bedroom courtyard house on a working farm featuring three pitched gables, reclaimed sandstone cladding and over 4000 reclaimed bricks from demolished steading buildings, with sinusoidal red agricultural-style cladding and extensive glazing connecting interior spaces to the private courtyard.

name: The Maker's House
description: A reunified stone villa in a conservation area with a new concrete extension featuring a roof light, insulation, and on-site heat pump, designed to serve as both family home and working studio.

name: The Carpenter's House
description: A B-listed former carpenter's house with parged red sandstone rubble walls, ballachulish slate and red pantile roof, and crow-step gables, refurbished and extended with a standing seam metal roof extension featuring large-format glazing to connect living spaces to the walled garden.

name: Strone of Glenbanchor
description: A refurbished and extended former crofter's cottage featuring original rubble stone walls and slate roof combined with timber-clad extensions, designed as a light-filled mountain retreat with views toward the Cairngorms.

name: The Origami House
description: An extension and internal reconfiguration of a Scottish cottage in a conservation village, featuring a 15 square metre addition with a folded pitched roof, Douglas fir window seat, exposed timber structure, and neutral natural materials including soft white walls and light microcement flooring.

name: The Shieling
description: A historic cottage renovation and extension in a conservation area featuring a folding roof with glass clerestory, birch ply interiors, slate flooring, and sliding glazing to frame views of the Campsie Fells.

name: Kingsborough Gardens
description: An extension and internal reconfiguration of a B-listed townhouse in Glasgow's conservation area, featuring a modern addition in large format wet cast concrete and weathering steel that connects the kitchen and living spaces to the back garden, with new staircases, underfloor heating, and improved insulation.

name: Of the Hill
description: A new build house on a hillside overlooking the Scottish coastline, made of prevailing landscape materials with a stone wall emerging from the hillside that forms an enclosed garden.

name: Gable House
description: A new build family home in rural Perthshire designed to reference historic gable forms on the site, featuring open living spaces with rural views, timber throughout, and Passivhaus standards.

name: The Equine House
description: A 155 square metre family home on a subdivided dairy farm featuring a striking red aluminium-framed window seat, black-stained larch cladding, white render, triple glazing, and sustainable systems including an air source heat pump and recycled aluminium roof.

name: Fan House
description: A transformed 1930s semi-detached four-bedroom house featuring a slanting wraparound extension with Douglas fir beams, large windows, oak veneer cabinetry, and a monolithic grey exterior that blends with the local landscape.

name: Pitch House
description: A new family home built on a hillside in rural Perthshire, formed from former agricultural sheds with an undulating roof pitch and constructed with highly insulated SIPs panels, preserving views across a courtyard to the landscape.

name: Cairnconon Byre
description: A contemporary single-family home built on the East Coast of Scotland that reuses reclaimed stone from an existing ruinous byre, featuring an L-shaped plan with polished concrete floors, floor-to-ceiling windows, and a sinusoidal metal roof inspired by local agricultural buildings.

name: Dulnain House
description: A contemporary home composed of two linked volumes—one in recycled granite stone and one in charred timber—designed to honor the site's history while incorporating passive systems and responding to modern climate realities.

name: Omata Beach House
description: A beachside residential house designed by Herbst Architects that won multiple NZIA architecture awards in 2023 for housing design.

name: Onetangi Cliff house
description: A beach house carved into the base of a cliff on Waiheke Island, recognized as Coastal Home of the Year 2025.

name: Dune House
description: A seaside residential project by Herbst Architects that won a 2022 HERE award for interior architecture, featuring collaboration with structural engineering, landscaping, and custom furniture design.

name: Lantern House Waiheke
description: A primary residence on a steep coastal slope featuring a two-level design with living spaces on the lower level stretched along the land contour and guest accommodation on the upper level, articulated by a continuous window seat and sheltered courtyard.

name: Kawakawa House Piha
description: A year-round beach house designed to maximize ocean views and natural light on a challenging sun-limited site, featuring an upper-level living area with continuous clerestory windows, open central courtyard, and covered deck overlooking Pohutukawa trees and mountains.

name: Bethells Bach
location: Te Henga (Bethells), 30km North-West of Auckland City
description: A two-bedroom bach overlooking a hillside, clad in vertical cedar boards that wrap inside, featuring a covered deck with fireplace, semi-enclosed rear terrace, timber batten screens, and a central courtyard with volcanic rocks.

name: K Valley House
description: A retreat for filmmakers on 20 hectares of farmland, clad in a rainscreen of rusted corrugated iron sheets and constructed largely from recycled materials and fittings, with a singular geometric form positioned straddling the ridgeline.

name: Muriwai House
description: A family dwelling sited within an existing copse of nikau palms on the West Coast.

name: Bay of Islands House
description: A house overlooking the Bay of Islands designed by Herbst Architects.

name: Omaha Beach House
description: A beach house located at Omaha, designed by Herbst Architects.

name: Bramasole House
description: A residential house on a former market garden and vineyard site in Waimauku, featuring three box-form elements clad in weathered timber with a central living pavilion, gabion basket walls dividing the site, and elevated on a blockwork plinth.

name: Castle Rock Beach House
description: A beach house featuring blunt, uncompromising materials designed to age naturally, with open spaces that invite sand and weathering as part of its distinctive sense of place.

name: Te Modular
description: A small bach (holiday shelter) design of 87m2 developed as a repeatable model that distills essential elements for a magical holiday home while controlling costs and size, built traditionally by local builders with only minor site modifications.

name: Under Pohutukawa
description: A beach house designed as a sympathetically placed pavilion that nestles among pohutukawa trees, featuring an opened-up summer configuration and executed with perfectionist precision to harmonize structure with its natural setting.

name: Bark House
description: A family home on a heavily wooded site with boldly executed forms using a limited palette of natural materials, designed to take advantage of limited vistas while bringing an urban edge to a rural setting.

name: Paremoremo House
description: A house on an undulating lifestyle block organized around a central courtyard bounded by cedar-shuttered pavilions on three sides, with views toward open landscape on the fourth side.

name: Inside out Bach
description: A summer holiday house with a linear plan transformed into individual spaces by a covered outdoor deck, sun court, and seating areas, featuring block piers, double timber posts, delicate trusses, and translucent walls that enclose private terraces.

name: Kaitoke Bach
description: A timber and glass retreat organized with a simple orthogonal plan, featuring layered screens, shady verandahs, and warm interior finishes contrasting with bleached natural exterior materials of timber and stone.

name: Oruawharo Bay Bach
description: A bach featuring a restrained palette of raw materials including a solid gabion wall, double columns, and timber boxes with generous openings, timber batten cladding, and rough gabion walls that create changing shadow play throughout the day.

name: Hammerhead House
description: A seaside bach featuring a crisp wooden box on a concrete block base, with living areas on the first floor connected to a terrace by exterior stair, bedrooms in the concrete base, and an animated exterior envelope created by robust timber detailing and movable sunscreen devices.

name: Wonderview House
description: A hybrid house/bach designed for a young couple featuring a rectilinear spiral block wall foundation anchoring the building into steep landscape, with a lightweight one-bedroom bach cantilevering over the plinth, oriented toward southern views with a north-facing roof opening for sunlight.

name: Aotea Bach
description: A pavilion-style bach on Great Barrier Island with two open sides allowing the landscape to flow through, featuring a south terrace on a shallow slope and a north deck overlooking an olive grove.

name: Herbst Bach
description: An experimental minimal bach featuring a room, veranda, and essential ablution facilities with lockable cupboards and sliding screens for security and weathering protection.

name: Pouaka Waikura Rust Sheds
description: A rural residential compound of four robust rectilinear pavilions clad in off-form concrete, Corten steel, and blackened steel joinery, designed for wine-making and car restoration on a 1.8-hectare terraced site overlooking the Shotover River.

name: Fendalton House
description: A two-level contemporary home with a white triple-gabled roof built on the footprint of a 1910 house destroyed in the 2011 Christchurch earthquake, featuring a central entry hallway with an eight-metre ceiling, full-height garden openings, a sculptural spiral staircase, and a passenger lift, designed to honor the spatial relationships of the original home while celebrating the owners' art collection and antique furniture.

name: Maungakawa
description: A radially symmetrical family home clad in custom orange plantation-grown renewable timber with on-site water harvesting and wastewater treatment, designed to echo the calm of a Gordon Walters painting and situated in a forest clearing overlooking the Waikato farmlands.

name: Olive Grove
description: A residential home surrounded by an existing olive grove on west-facing slopes, featuring a two-way spanning cantilevered timber roof that shelters a multi-purpose room, changing rooms, and north-facing terrace overlooking a swimming pool and tennis court.

name: Swan Lake
description: A 705m2 private residence constructed in rusted core 10 steel, skim rendered brickwork, and aluminium pivoting joinery, centered around a courtyard with an artificial infinity-edged reflection lake and sculptural hillocks framing views of Coronet Peak and the Wakatipu landscape.

name: Wanaka Lodge
description: A sun-oriented residential lodge crafted in local schist stone with two large pavilions enclosing a private courtyard, designed to reference a Southern Italian masseria while reflecting the surrounding Southern Alps landscape.

name: Black Peak / Mount Burke
description: A light timber-framed house on the shore of Lake Wanaka with charred larch cladding and a local stone plinth, designed as two pavilions (main home and guest house) aligned to mountain views, with the kitchen as a central hub for both intimate and extended family living.

name: Local Rock House
description: A New Zealand coastal residence for an expatriate family on a steep escarpment, featuring a prominent rock mass structure that creates living areas nestled into the landscape with a northern terrace and western courtyard, using local materials to integrate with its setting above a pohutukawa-fringed beach.

name: Scrubby Bay House
description: A robust farmhouse set on a remote coastal sheep and cattle station, featuring a vernacular form with macrocarpa timber interior, a central stone fireplace built from quarried station rock, and custom-designed steel fittings and furnishings.

name: Pines House
description: A family bach composed of zinc-clad pavilions arranged around pine trees, featuring a long front deck with views, corrugated zinc cladding extending into the interior, and a sloping sylvan courtyard, with the beach in front.

name: Waiheke House
description: A residential pavilion on a sloped site with a sculptural timber-clad roof suspended above extensively glazed living and sleeping areas, an embedded in situ concrete base containing services, and a geometrically-matched swimming pool integrated into the landscape.

name: Boat Shed Bay
description: A secluded holiday home comprising three connected pavilions arranged around a north-facing courtyard, featuring roof forms and board and batten cladding that echo historic boatsheds nearby.

name: Naisoso Island
description: A new tropical home built with local trade block, in-situ plastered concrete, and imported aluminium joinery with security fins that function as storm shutters and sun shades, featuring a coral stone wall and white interior on cool concrete floors.

name: Mai Mai
description: A home for a couple featuring white fibreglass exterior walls with a feathery motif referencing traditional Māori cloaks, and interior spaces including a glass-surrounded sitting room, leather-lined den, and interior courtyard with city views.

name: Parihoa
description: A contemporary rural house positioned on a wind-swept coastal hill with black stained exterior boards and timber interiors, designed as a fortress-like structure that wraps around a protected circulation courtyard while preserving the surrounding landscape.

name: Seagrass House
description: A robust beachfront house clad in corbelled brickwork that reflects the colors and textures of the surrounding rocky headland, designed to withstand bushfire risk while featuring spaces suspended in trees overlooking the beach.

name: Annandale House
description: A contemporary family home set behind an existing weatherboard cottage, featuring interlocking brick masonry volumes arranged like telescope tubes to maximize light, air, and open space for a busy family of four.

name: Albert Street
description: A house featuring a precast concrete culvert creating street presence, with sequences of external and internal spaces using timber and off-form concrete in their natural state, and a floating roof with three-sided clerestory for natural light and seasonal views.

name: Twin Set
description: A semi-detached house expanded into its twin to accommodate a large family, reoriented around a central garden courtyard with concrete cassettes and a new pavilion framing the courtyard and living spaces.

name: Hordern Street
description: An alteration to an inner-city house featuring a steel-framed addition clad with pre-cast concrete panel off-cuts, with a pitched roof designed to capture light while maintaining privacy and respecting the adjacent sandstone stable wall and cottage.

name: House 6
description: A terrace house renovation that adds 6 square metres of space to the rear through selective replacement of elements, creating flexible spaces that respond to occupants' needs.

name: Venus Bay House
description: A modest, cost-effective beach house built from corrugated metal, fibre cement sheet, plywood and galvanised steel, featuring sustainable systems including photovoltaic cells, solar hot water, rainwater tanks and on-site blackwater treatment.

name: Greybox
description: A courtyard house designed for outdoor living, featuring a 3-sided verandah wrapping around a central courtyard with separate rooms, inspired by homestead, beachside motel, tractor shed, and abbey typologies.

name: Rockbound
description: A residential house that emerges from rocky terrain with primary living spaces parallel to the water, featuring naturally weathering materials and panoramic views toward Peggy's Cove Lighthouse.

name: OG House
description: A residential project in Halifax's North End featuring a primary residence for the architect above a ground-floor community studio dedicated to neighborhood projects including housing for the homeless and public amenities.

name: White Rock
description: A 1,500 sqft residential house perched above a steep rocky incline overlooking the Gaspereau River Valley, completed in summer 2023.

name: Jib House
description: A residential house on a triangular coastal lot in Chester Village with south-facing views overlooking the Chester basin and nearby islands.

name: Fyren
description: A residential beacon set atop a high sea-side plateau in the Halifax area with an L-shaped scheme that twists toward views of Point Pleasant Park and open water, featuring an internal court and multiple viewing zones.

name: Harbour Heights
description: A minimalist cedar-clad residential house with a gable design overlooking Inverness Harbour, featuring a single-storey presentation from the main road and a second storey of glass and cedar cladding on the hillside side, with the main living spaces on the entrance level.

name: Black Gables
description: Two modest gabled residential buildings with jet black exteriors and metal roofs, positioned at skewed angles to optimize views and daylighting, featuring a private side with expansive glazing overlooking the landscape and seascape, and a public-facing dark façade with minimal glazing for privacy.

name: Shantih
description: A residential refuge composed of contrasting identities with two arms wrapping around sloping land toward the sea, described as modest yet elaborate and finely crafted.

name: The Lookout at Broad Cove Marsh
description: A 2,000 sqft residential house situated on a narrow coastal lot between a tree-lined road and ocean cliff, designed for a Toronto couple as a family retreat with expansive sunset views over the Gulf of St. Lawrence.

name: Teph Inlet
description: A summer home composed of three rectilinear volumes with red cedar-clad horizontal boards on the main house and a glass-encased ground level, featuring massive sliding glass panels opening to a pool and deck, with an adjacent pool house and aluminum panel-clad garage.

name: Rabbit Snare Gorge
description: A residential cabin built on a steeply-gorged property in Cape Breton with historical significance to the client's family, who had used the land for rabbit snaring and laundry washing.

name: Brar Residence
description: A 3000 sqft residential home designed to accommodate a family with two young daughters and the client's mother, prioritizing multi-generational living and accessibility.

name: Lake Joseph Cottage
description: A gable-form residence on a small island featuring a heavy stone band anchoring the structure to exposed granite, with a peaked wood volume above, using local stone, dark wood siding, and dark metals to blend into the surrounding pine forest environment.

name: Schlotfeldt Residence
description: A corten-clad house situated high above the Okanagan valley within the mountain landscape, designed to resemble a land ship.

name: Treow Brycg
description: A fortress-like residential structure with a canted back shell inspired by local gambrel-roofed barns, situated on Kingsburg Beach and designed to withstand unpredictable Nova Scotian weather.
A reimagined family home situated on a hilltop property north of Lake Ontario, overlooking natural features including a creek, pond, maple grove, and treed woodlot.

name: Sluice Point
description: A residential house located on a forested high point in southern Nova Scotia with views of marshland, islands, and the Tusket River.

name: Float
description: A residential home in Halifax's Purcell's Cove inspired by the dramatic glacial landscape of jagged bedrock, overlooking lakes and the ocean.

name: Syncline
description: A quiet, masculine modern residential home located in south end Halifax on a geological syncline, overlooking the North-West Arm adjacent to Point Pleasant Park.

name: Leaf House
description: A residential sanctuary beside a natural spring featuring a curved roof shell inspired by organic leaf forms, expansive windows framing water and forest views, and seamlessly integrated indoor-outdoor spaces.

name: East River
description: A residential house situated along Nova Scotia's rugged shoreline, conceived for a couple relocating from Montreal seeking a life more deeply rooted in nature and defined by the presence of the Atlantic.

name: Cedar's Kin
description: A residential home nestled into a cedar forest on a steep hillside, organized as interconnected volumes that step down toward the water to engage the landscape at multiple elevations.

name: Yo-Ju Courtyard House
description: A single-family residence in the Clyde Hill neighborhood that creates privacy through a series of thresholds from opaque to transparent, blending ancient principles with modern design while adjacent to a busy arterial street.

name: Aldo Beach House
description: A transformed 1940s beach house that doubles the livable area for multi-generational use, featuring two shifting wings hovering over the hillside supported by thin steel columns and pin piles while minimizing impact on the waterfront ecology.

name: Grasshopper Studio
description: A studio and guesthouse for a family with three small children, built primarily of recycled materials, with the main house and studio linked by a covered breezeway that integrates landscape and architecture around a private courtyard.

name: Hood Cliff Retreat
description: A family retreat comprising a repurposed 1962 cabin, new addition, and bunkhouse, featuring a material palette of marble, oak, cedar, and terrazzo, with indoor-outdoor kitchen connections and high clerestory windows designed to connect occupants with the Puget Sound ecosystem.

name: Capitol Hill Courtyard Garden
description: A single-family residence featuring interconnected gardens at multiple levels, including a central courtyard with Stewartia trees, sedum green roofs with Lake Washington views, and landscape elements such as silver vein Parthenocissus vines on concrete walls and basalt pavers through planted beds.

name: Whidbey Puzzle Prefab
description: A prefab house that merges high-performance sustainability with customizable, site-responsive design, achieving carbon-negative performance while maintaining craft detail.

name: Whidbey Uparati
description: A 1,880 square foot meditation retreat with two bedrooms and two bathrooms that floats above a meadow, minimizing its visual and physical impact on the land through a wood-focused design that blends into the site.

name: French Creek Workshops
description: A new family retreat nestled alongside a wetland featuring a courtyard composed of living spaces and workshops for weaving, glass blowing, and furniture making, with a roof designed to turn rainwater into garden pools.

name: Wenatchee River Cabin
description: A one-bedroom retreat built of concrete and steel that balances shelter and nature while serving as a basecamp for outdoor adventures in proximity to the Wenatchee River and Okanogan Wenatchee National Forest.

name: Blakely Island Cabin
description: A 400 square foot guest cabin suspended on stilts within a forest on the Salish Sea, featuring a small kitchen, murphy bed, bathroom, and loft with bunks, designed in the tradition of minimalist retreats like Walden Cabin.

name: The Hideaway
description: An art collector's weekend house perched on a rocky outcrop overlooking a remote mountain lake, cantilevering within the trees to balance privacy and expansive views.

name: Casa Santa María
description: A residential house designed by Felipe Assadi and Jorge Manieu in Santiago, Chile, featuring notable use of red timber (timbre rojo) as a distinctive material.

name: Casa Serrano
description: A residential house designed by Felipe Assadi and Christophe Rousselle in Santiago, Chile.

name: Casa H
description: A reinforced concrete structure composed of longitudinal and transverse beams supporting a ceiling slab with 7-meter cantilevers, featuring open-plan living spaces and a pool volume that extends toward the sea.

name: Casa Remota
description: An 80-square-meter prefabricated modular transportable house with three bedrooms, two bathrooms, and integrated living/dining/kitchen space, constructed from four identical modules with an iron chassis clad in pinewood inside and out.

name: Knarrvika 2.0
description: A summer house elevated on expressive posts with a two-level volume, featuring asphalt roofing and black-stained cladding, designed to sit lightly on ground between a disused quarry and bedrock.

name: Knarrvika 1.0
description: A coastal cabin with a concrete base and two stepped volumes clad in Corten steel, featuring deep window reveals facing the Oslo fjord and birch plywood interiors.

name: Villa Sandnes
description: An inward-facing house organized around a central courtyard with a circular roof opening that tracks the sun, featuring brick external walls and paving, raw concrete ceilings, smooth wooden floors, and perforated timber screens.

name: Villa Fuglenesseter
description: A single-family villa composed of two volumes arranged in a courtyard farmyard form alongside a 300-year-old barn, with a glulam wood skeleton, locally sourced pine exterior treated with iron vitriol, and interior plywood wall panels that serve as ornamentation.

name: Villa Furuholmen
description: A single-family villa on an archipelago site composed of small volumes raised on stilts and linked by terraces, designed to minimize disturbance to the exposed cliffs, junipers, and lichen landscape.

name: Strandhuset
description: A guest lodge raised on stilts at the forest edge with a flexible interior plan featuring oak floorboards, solid oak windows, white-painted pine cladding, and a timber wall construction without plastics or adhesives.

name: Villa Verde
description: A two-storey villa on a steep mountainside with an elongated form set along the slope, featuring bedrooms on the enclosed lower floor, living spaces that open above into a winter garden, and materials of untreated timber, grey render, concrete, Douglas fir, and cross-laminated timber.

name: Villa Bjerkelund
description: A two-storey family home in brick, zinc, and metal with oak floors, timber window frames, and a brick fireplace, designed for permanence and to age well through quality materials and careful composition.

name: House and Studio in Kyoto
description: An atelier and residence in Kyoto designed by Tato Architects.

name: Roof Slider/Napping corridor-Kagerou Village
description: A single-dwelling residence designed by Tato Architects, featuring a sloped roof corridor suitable for napping.

name: House in Suwayama
location: Making the Surrounding Environment a Compositional Element of Space

name: House in Kurekawatyou
description: A residential house designed by Tato Architects / Yo Shimada.

name: Casa SSG
description: A three-volume residential compound in the Treviso countryside featuring a prominent roof design, fluid interior spaces with large glazed openings, and varying interior heights that frame views across the landscape.

name: CASA DLS
description: A two-level house with underground level designed around a central cast-in-place concrete wall that organizes spaces, features simple lines and authentic materials, with the ground floor containing living areas and kitchen opening to a garden, and upper level with three bedrooms.

name: Casa Roveri
description: A restored terraced house originally dating from the early 1800s in Treviso's Fiera district, formerly part of a rural villa complex, featuring original wooden staircases and floors, with a narrow garden and cautious interventions that preserved historical elements while creating more intimate bedroom spaces.

name: Casa BC
description: A restored early 1900s two-storey house with attic (240 sqm) featuring a converted garage roof terrace and private courtyard, with exposed iron structure, microcement and oak wood floors, and black iron architectural elements.

name: Casa 2x1
description: A merged two-unit residence featuring an open ground floor with kitchen, dining room, and living room, and an upper floor with bedrooms, guest room, and studio, unified by clear large-tile flooring that creates brightness and spatial continuity.

name: Casa Fiera
description: A restored historic house in Treviso's Porto di Fiera district with a modern wooden-clad addition, featuring recovered original roof beams and new openings framing views of the adjacent Sant'Ambrogio church.

name: Hollow Water
description: A contemporary new build house on a steeply sloping site in rural Devon, with a three-part form clad in copper roofs, granite walls, and waney-edge Douglas fir timber milled from trees felled on site, designed to respond to the landscape's natural contours and local vernacular.

name: Peckham House
description: A contemporary infill new build single-family house featuring a monolithic form clad in hit-and-miss brickwork, with a low-carbon high-performance envelope including triple glazing, MVHR, air source heat pump, and photovoltaics, and interior materials including terrazzo, English larch, and experimental lime and gypsum plasters.

name: Clock Tower House
description: A six-storey vertical house on a compact urban infill site in central London, featuring a material palette of stone, Portland stone brick, and glazing, with a distinctive double-height glazed clock face, rooftop terrace with panoramic Thames views, and low-carbon structural innovations including calcined clay concrete and air source heat pump.

name: Bury Gate Farm
description: A new single-family residence replacing a 1950s bungalow, designed as a modern villa within a parkland setting, featuring a two-storey colonnade and constructed with handmade brickwork, rammed concrete, and precast concrete elements.

name: Monkton
description: A new 4-bedroom multigenerational house featuring a rectilinear ground floor plan with three bedroom towers at first floor with mono-pitch roofs, stepped to follow the site slope and provide increasingly generous ceiling heights in living spaces.

name: Slot House
description: A highly crafted 2-storey 1-bed house constructed within a narrow 2.8m wide gap between existing terraces using a lightweight steel frame with fully welded portal frames and handmade pewter glazed tile cladding.

name: South Street, Lewes
description: A four-bedroom house on a brownfield site in the South Downs National Park with an in-situ concrete frame infilled with local ash-glazed brickwork at ground level and CorTen steel cladding above that weathers to ochre, referencing the site's industrial heritage.

name: Dangstein Estate
description: A substantial new country house with poolhouse and gatehouse featuring bespoke cyclopean masonry walls made from Fittleworth Stone boulders embedded in lime, GGBS, and local stone aggregate, organized around a central courtyard linking to historic estate elements.

name: Housestead
description: A new countryside house where daily and yearly living functions are broken down into simplified components and expressed as separate buildings.

name: Contour House
description: A contemporary family home organized linearly along a contour, constructed with local stone flowing seamlessly from walls to roof, designed to frame landscape views and embed sustainable design principles.

name: The Narrow House
description: A private residence built on a single garage footprint between neighboring properties, featuring a simple internal circulation organized around a laser-cut stair with morse code shipping forecast, designed to display the owners' artwork and sculpture collection.

name: Reciprocal House
description: A residential extension and coach house replacement in Hampstead that retains and upgrades a 1968 Foster Associates extension, featuring an optimised exposed concrete structure, perforated aluminium sail-like roofs, and highly crafted aluminium interior elements that echo the minimalist material approach of the original.

name: Casa Kiké
description: A private house and writing studio comprising two timber pavilions raised on piles, designed to house a library of 17,000 books, a writing desk, and a grand piano, with glazed ends oriented to catch northerly sea breezes and constructed using locally sourced materials.

name: House in a Garden
description: A new single-family house replacing a 1960s bungalow, featuring a copper-clad pavilion with a complex double-curved glulam timber roof, two underground stories including bedrooms and a swimming pool, and extensive use of light wells and skylights to bring daylight deep into the earth-sheltered design.

name: Light House
description: An 800 m² family house in Notting Hill with an inverted section placing bedrooms on the ground floor and living spaces on the first floor, featuring a completely glazed 'sky facade' roof with variable fritting densities designed as an environmental moderator based on detailed solar and daylight analysis.

name: Simple House
description: A modest 85m² infill house featuring exposed timber joists, rough brick perimeter walls, exposed aggregate concrete paving, and a central tall airy hall with courtyards on either side, designed on a tight budget to demonstrate that a small house can offer delight.

name: Lochside House
description: An off-grid, energy-efficient house featuring highly-insulated SIP panels, Scottish larch cladding charred using the shou sugi ban technique, a modular three-volume form with pitched roofs, and sustainable systems for water, sewage, and electrical needs.

name: Meadowbank
description: A comprehensive sustainable retrofit of an existing 1960s house featuring additional insulation, timber cladding, a wood pellet boiler, mechanical ventilation with heat recovery, solar panels, a two-storey conservatory, and rainwater harvesting.

name: Elm End
description: A contemporary asymmetric house on the North Norfolk Coast clad in cedar boards with three linked volumes, flat roofs with terraces, vertical timber staves providing privacy to windows, and sustainable features including solar panels and mechanical ventilation heat recovery.

name: Accessible House
description: A new accessible house for a couple and visiting children with live-in carer accommodation, featuring a barn-like character with glulam roof trusses, microcement and cork flooring, wheelchair-accessible design including a lift and hoist runs, and a private west-facing courtyard garden with olive trees and water features.

name: The Knoll
description: A contemporary extension to a sixteenth-century farmhouse featuring a new kitchen, library with vaulted ceiling overlooking an enlarged pond, and utility spaces, built with custom-manufactured Bourn Great Bricks to match the historic nineteenth-century fabric.

name: Stone Cottage
description: A retrofit and extension of a 19th century Suffolk farm worker's cottage featuring a new two-storey extension, panoramic south-facing views, solar-panel pergola, traditional flint and brick walls, and decarbonisation improvements to meet modern sustainability targets.

name: Coast House
description: An award-winning contemporary single-family home in Norfolk featuring a Corten steel-framed main living space with a sedum roof, knapped-flint staggered walls, triple glazing, and Passivhaus technologies including solar panels, battery storage, and an air source heat pump.

name: Bavent House
description: A coastal family home with a U-shaped plan around a south-facing courtyard, featuring black zinc cladding and weathered Iroko timber, designed to shelter from North Sea winds while capturing views across reed marshes, with ground source heat pump heating and recycled newspaper wall insulation.

name: Jersey House
description: A contemporary new family home overlooking St Ouen's Bay that replaces a bungalow, featuring a half-level stepped design into the landscape, extensive south-facing glazing for solar gain, solar panels, heat recovery system, and a roof overhang designed for seasonal solar optimization.

name: The Eyrie
description: A contemporary new family home with a steeped pitch roof providing internal volume, open-plan living spaces, prefabricated timber-frame construction, photovoltaics, ground source heat pump with underfloor heating, and materials informed by local vernacular architecture.

name: South Cliff
description: A coastal family home on a steeply sloping site with two floors, featuring off-white brick and red grandis timber cladding, large south-facing glazing with sea views, stepped terraces descending to the beach, and sustainable systems including an air source heat pump and solar array.

name: Beach End & Seascape
description: Two new build houses on the beachfront with three floors, open plan living spaces on the top floor maximizing views, three double bedrooms with balconies, built with Petersen Tegl linear white and black bricks, and featuring heat pumps with solar arrays and battery storage achieving EPC A100 rating.

name: Lapwings (The Suttons)
description: A newly built beach house featuring fair-faced concrete structural elements and cedar cladding, designed with ground source heating, solar panels, and high insulation to withstand the coastal environment while maximizing views across the beach to the English Channel.

name: Shishiodoshi House
description: A vertical wood-frame house with white PVC membrane cladding designed for a young family of five, featuring an oversized aluminum Japanese shishiodoshi rainwater feature and large cantilevered balconies.

name: 5.6 House
description: A coastal house in Brittany entirely built in concrete and granite, featuring multiple patios and individual bedrooms with en-suite bathrooms opening onto sandy courtyards, with long sun-screens evoking the wooden beach markers of the coastal landscape.

name: (((db))) house
description: A white parallelepiped residence organized around a central swimming pool, featuring scaled cladding on the north facade and extensive glazing on the south, creating a flexible boundary between interior and exterior spaces.

name: house of the choir
description: A single-story house stretching along a narrow lot with a central street and lateral patios, featuring pivoting partition doors for flexible spaces, a pearlescent white exterior with metallic reflections, and an attached shed functioning as a workshop-cellar and garage.

name: patchwork à la flotte
description: A tall residential villa featuring a sculptural wooden interior partition with patchwork wood cladding, containing lofted bedrooms accessible by a massive staircase, overlooking the living space and garden with sea views.

name: All Out House
description: A villa with a 35-meter main facade alternating between glazed, solid, and perforated walls, featuring a thick solar shading element above and interior spaces organized around a central patio that connects to a south-facing garden.

name: le début des enduits
description: A single-family house elevated to prevent flooding, featuring a simple cubic volumetry with industrial steel framing, double-height interiors with galleries, and infill panels with a patchwork of stucco finishes mimicking neighboring buildings.

name: C'est non choix
description: A semi-buried, minimalist house with smooth self-placing concrete walls and a PVC membrane roof, stripped of ornamentation and architectural details.

name: topless house
description: A 50 m² vacation house addition on the Atlantic coast featuring a removable roof, polished concrete terrace, sliding glass corner doors, and a kitchen counter extending 7 meters toward a bedroom designed as a small house with a pitched roof.

name: Twist House
description: A single-family residence in central Nantes with a sculptural twisted volumetry across 4 levels, featuring a white lacquered horizontal wood cladding, concrete frame structure, and a ribbon-like staircase, designed to respond to the sloped terrain and preserve existing trees.

name: La maison du Coteau
description: A family house clad in wood with specific implementations on all sides, positioned 70 meters above the Loire River, featuring bedrooms designed as camera obscuras with pixelated beveled wooden cube frames and motorized textile blinds.

name: Maison presque parfaite
description: An adaptation of a 1990s family vacation home on Ré Island, proposing the addition of dressing spaces, custom furniture, and interior painting to create buffer zones and improved functionality for multiple generations, though the project was ultimately not realized due to family disagreements over modifications.

name: Maison bleue
description: A primary residence designed with an inverted color hierarchy featuring anthracite gray walls and a light white-blue roof, oriented rigorously North/South with selective window placement for climate control and spatial flow that blurs the boundaries between rooms.

name: Maison Laffitte
description: A miniature castle-like residence on a 10,000 square meter plot, featuring a central body with two symmetrical wings housing children's and owner's apartments with reception salons, organized by a 4.40 m module and accompanied by a reflecting pool.

name: Maison cardio
description: A vacation house designed to become a family residence for a large sports-oriented family, with 190 m² of living space plus 45 m² of terrace, built in a suburban residential development.

name: Bella vita
description: A residential house featuring a monolithic blind facade with a transparent polycarbonate garage door that acts as sculptural street presence, opening generously on the garden side with a 10-meter bay window, terraced area supported by concrete columns, and an elevated swimming pool accessible via a monumental staircase.

name: Le Roc
description: A 131 m² micro-architecture house with stone construction on the ground floor, characterized by a 7.50m bay window with 9 panels, high ceilings (5.35m) in bedrooms, and symmetrical façades, designed to minimize circulation while accommodating a dining area, fireplace, three bedrooms, and pool on a sloped hillside site.

name: Maison Mouvaux
description: A family house nestled at the edge of a wooded site with soft forms and materiality reflecting the surrounding nature, featuring an amplified roof that dominates the design while the ground floor disappears beneath roof overhangs and landscape reflections in faceted surfaces.

name: Black House
description: A sculptural timber-frame house clad in anthracite zinc, organized around a central living space opening onto agricultural landscape with lateral service zones and a cantilevered upper floor with planted terraces, referencing the black-clad agricultural buildings of the region.

name: Little House
description: A modest single-family house in Arras with a simple wooden frame structure and extensive glazing on three sides, designed to maximize spatial richness and views despite tight budget constraints, situated on a sloped narrow lot with a wooden boardwalk along the south facade.

name: Pile ou Face
description: A house with interior spaces organized along a cross-plan, featuring a glass ground floor, a light-giving patio, a cantilever bedroom terrace, and dark, massive volumes designed to emphasize the void beneath and enhance the sense of levitation.

name: Airstream House
description: A three-part single-family residence inspired by Airstream caravans and streamline design, organized across split-levels to work with the sloping terrain, featuring aluminum cladding and extensive glazing that frames views of open countryside.

name: Maison dans un champ
description: A 180 m² family house with a wooden shell structure featuring cedar shingle and charred northern pine exterior cladding, birch plywood and local ash interior, heated by a mass stove with passive solar heating and no electrical connection.

name: Maison dans le Pré
