description: A small 90 m² wooden-frame house designed for a large family with a budget of €125,000, featuring Douglas pine structure, zinc standing-seam roof, larch and polycarbonate sliding panels, wood fiber insulation, and wood stove heating, where the exposed wooden structure organizes all interior spaces without additional walls or partitions.

name: Le Kiosque
description: A 110 m² house designed as a sheltered garden pavilion, featuring a natural zinc standing-seam roof with generous overhangs, a wood platform on concrete beams and steel micropiles, local sapwood framing, larch cladding and joinery, hemp brick and earth plaster interior partitions, and wood fiber insulation with wood stove heating.

name: Maison devant la Dune
description: A 66 m² wooden house designed to enjoy the dunes and sea while protected from strong coastal winds, featuring half exterior unheated open-air space and half heated interior, with a black larch wood envelope, wood wool insulation, and wood-burning stove heating.

name: Maison sur le Mur
description: A 132 m² single-family house organized along a preserved street-facing boundary wall, featuring a double-pitched red pigmented zinc roof, larch wood slatted ventilation screens, black pine resin-treated wood cladding, wood fiber insulation, and a common living space designed as an observatory of the surrounding orchards.

name: Maison Traversée
description: A 110 m² house built on a steep slope featuring two stacked boxes in different orientations, constructed with concrete foundations, northern spruce, standing-seam zinc, Douglas pine, and charred spruce, with wood wool insulation and a mass heater.

name: Maison dans la Forêt
description: A 200 m² house in a forest clearing featuring larch cladding and concrete foundations, with layered transparent and opaque elements designed to blur the boundary between interior and forest landscape.

name: Maison dans le Jardin
description: A 130 m² compact house featuring concrete foundations, northern spruce, larch boards, and clear/screened glass, with wood wool insulation and a wood stove, designed to integrate sensitively with an existing garden through low rooflines and modular cladding.

name: Maison dans la Prairie
description: A 78 m² house designed for two people using minimal, basic construction with northern spruce, steel sheeting, and larch cladding, featuring sliding larch-framed windows that open onto prairie views and employing wood heating, solar passive design, and dry toilets.

name: La Halle
description: A family residence designed as a variation on a Norman hall, featuring a concrete basement with northern spruce, larch cladding, slate roof, and wood fiber insulation, combining the main house with office and storage spaces within a monumental four-pitched roof structure.

name: Maison Cosse
description: A 176 m² house designed for an opera singer and family, featuring a larch wood shell envelope enclosing the living spaces across three levels, with wood fiber insulation, wood stove heating, and passive solar orientation toward the south while screening street views.

name: L'Onde
description: A 75 m² house with a distinctive flexible, curved roof (convex on the south side, concave on the north) clad in black pre-patinated zinc standing seam and larch, featuring raw concrete flooring, exposed timber framing, and birch plywood interior elements.

name: Petite Maison
description: A minimal 20 m² residential dwelling with concrete plots, northern spruce, corrugated metal and polycarbonate, larch cladding, and wood-burning heat, designed to maximize connection to an existing garden and sea views through sliding window walls and a sea-facing bay window.

name: Maison près du Sapin
description: A 40 m² small house featuring a protective large roof sheltering a wooden platform, with double-height living space and interior finishes of OSB panels and spruce plywood, using northern spruce, red cedar shingles, larch joinery, and wood fiber insulation with wood stove heating.

name: Maison sur la Montagne
description: A 120 m² chalet-inspired house anchored into existing rock with a minimalist steel structure, featuring larch and polycarbonate sliding frames that open onto valley views, and finished with northern spruce, clay tiles, and wood fiber insulation.

name: La Grange
description: A 228 m² house with a traditional exterior matching village regulations, featuring a bright, open interior with double-height living spaces, wood fiber insulation, geothermal underfloor heating, and materials including concrete slab, northern pine, terracotta tiles, larch cladding, and polished concrete.

name: Maison Relais
description: A 175 m² wood-frame house featuring a sophisticated hollow brick wall system connected to a Canadian well and wood stove for thermal mass and passive heating/cooling, with materials including concrete foundations, northern pine, standing-seam zinc roofing, and larch cladding.

name: Maison Tube
description: A tubular-form single-family house with concrete foundations, northern softwood framing, vegetated roof, and wood wool insulation, featuring a heat pump and radiant floor heating system that deforms with the site's topography to maximize southern solar exposure while minimizing visual impact on neighboring properties.

name: Entre les murs
description: A 108 m² wooden house with pine tar-coated exterior and atrium interior, designed as an intervention behind an opening cut into an existing stone vine wall, with an external covered walkway connecting three gardens oriented to different sun exposures throughout the day.

name: Maison Corse
description: A small 17 m² residential structure designed as a shepherd's cabin with concrete foundations, Corsican pine, slate roofing, and larch cladding, featuring sliding glazed windows and an external walkway that creates a transition between interior and exterior spaces.

name: Papillon
description: A 100 m² house featuring polycarbonate and larch wood walls with manually articulated panels that open like butterfly wings to create shaded overhangs and expand the living space into the surrounding landscape.

name: Maison Bleue
description: A narrow townhouse with a simple carved-out volume featuring a central garden strip for privacy, blue rendered façade with wood-framed windows, and an open-plan interior with living spaces on the upper floor extending to a south-facing terrace.

name: Maison Noire
description: A wooden house with local chestnut wood cladding on a narrow urban lot, designed as a continuous volume with two interior patios to create privacy in a dense neighborhood context.

name: Maison Jumelles
description: Twin houses on a sensitive coastal site featuring bio-sourced materials including hemp concrete, natural earth plaster, and slate roofs, with ground floor socles and dissociated upper stories designed to integrate into regional architectural character.

name: Maison Lostoen
description: A single-story house renovation and extension featuring a slate roof with a distinctive wide overhang (lostoen), dark-colored render, wooden panels painted with agricultural oil to reveal wood grain, and integration into the landscape through reorientation and garden development.

name: Maison Terre
description: A seaside vacation house extension in Brittany that creates a twin dwelling connected to the existing pavilion, built primarily with rammed earth (pisé) and wood on a concrete base, designed to provide thermal efficiency while maintaining panoramic views of Cap d'Erquy.

name: Maison sur la pente
description: A single-family residence built on pilotis on a steeply sloped, forested site near Erquy bay, featuring solid wood construction with biobased insulation, generous roof overhangs, and a design that preserves the natural landscape and existing pine trees.

name: Maison Canal
description: A four-person house on a narrow urban lot featuring a mix of concrete and wood materials, with the structure set back from the street to create a front garden buffer, while the garden-facing side opens generously with a wooden structure and roof overhang for solar protection.
